speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how does LTA specify the methodology of traffic impact assessments, especially for new housing developments in mature estates; (b) whether the planning assumptions for traffic impact assessments assume a "car-lite" future; and (c) whether a range of vehicle population scenarios is considered when making such assessments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA publishes guidelines on how developers should conduct the TIAs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: First, developers should establish the baseline traffic demand before the development is built by carrying out a traffic survey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Developers also have to estimate the future growth in traffic volume due to external factors, such as the vehicle growth rate and other new developments in the area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Second, developers should assess the additional traffic that will be generated by the planned development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This is typically done via surveying a comparable development and adjusting for a lower vehicle mode share if there are future improvements in public transport and active mobility access to the development when it is ready.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some mature HDB estates had the road designs, especially the smaller loop roads, built at a time when vehicle norms were quite different from today.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: As a result, some residents are concerned when there are additional residential developments coming up, such as in the town of Clementi where I serve.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: What measures will the Ministry consider to, at least, ensure the vehicle congestion is moderated?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA does take into account relevant factors, such as new developments and road size, when making TIAs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As what Dr Tan mentioned in his supplementary question regarding size of old roads as well as potential congestion, as part of the TIA, the developer will have to identify the development's impact on the surrounding transport network and recommend necessary measures to mitigate some of these potential negative impact, including congestion, as mentioned by Dr Tan.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the second question on how we ensure safety for the pedestrian, whenever possible, LTA will work with URA to build overhead pedestrian networks so that the elderly do not have to cross the busy roads.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: When overhead link bridges are not possible or not appropriate, LTA will also identify Silver Zones to make our roads even safer for the elderly.
